forces.title: High financing costs cap residential construction momentum
forces.description: Elevated financing costs, particularly higher interest rates, significantly impact the residential development sector across Europe. They make new builds less affordable for buyers, who often finance payments during construction, and increase the cost of capital for developers. This dampens overall momentum, leading to cautious investment and project postponements, thus delaying a stronger residential recovery despite housing shortages in many cities.
forces.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

forces.title: Geopolitical risks heighten buyer reluctance for new homes
forces.description: Heightened geopolitical uncertainty, particularly from conflicts like the Iran war, contributes to buyer reluctance for new-build homes in Europe. The longer waiting periods for completion (up to two years) increase perceived uncertainty compared to buying existing properties. This reduced consumer confidence and caution acts as a significant headwind, capping momentum for residential development and stabilizing new building permit issuance.
forces.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

forces.title: Rising energy prices increase building material costs
forces.description: Higher energy prices are pushing up production costs for energy-intensive building materials like concrete, cement, and bricks across Europe. While the overall increase in construction costs has been modest so far, it exacerbates financial pressures on developers. This makes new projects less commercially viable, especially when developers struggle to pass these increased costs onto buyers who already face higher interest rates, leading to project delays or unprofitability.
forces.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

forces.title: Weak housing economics limit new build viability
forces.description: Weak housing economics, characterized by new-build prices often being higher than existing homes and limited scope for developers to pass on increased material costs, severely constrain the commercial viability of new residential projects in Europe. In countries like France, Germany, and Austria, existing home prices have risen less than the European average, making new builds comparatively expensive and leading developers to postpone construction until market conditions improve.
forces.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

forces.title: Policy uncertainty and rising duties dampen demand
forces.description: Policy uncertainty, such as the Flemish government's plan to raise registration duties on the sole family home from 2% to 3%, dampens housing demand in Belgium. This measure increases the anticipated costs of home purchases, making it more difficult for households to plan and potentially reducing overall demand, especially in a market already expected to lose momentum. Such policy shifts add to existing headwinds for residential development.
forces.source_title: Belgian building permit recovery continues, but challenges lie ahead

forces.title: Energy efficiency premium for homes driving demand
forces.description: Higher energy prices are widening the price gap between energy-efficient and energy-intensive homes in Belgium. Demand for energy-efficient homes is expected to remain relatively resilient as buyers increasingly value their financial benefits (reduced energy expenses) and hedge against future price shocks and regulatory risks. This creates an upside driver for developers focusing on high-performance, sustainable residential properties, as energy performance becomes a critical determinant of property value and marketability.
forces.source_title: Second-quarter resilience masks a more challenging outlook for Belgian housing

forces.title: Increased supply of existing homes moderating price growth
forces.description: A growing supply of existing homes, including a substantial share from investors selling rental properties into the owner-occupied market, is increasing buyer choice and reducing market tightness in the Netherlands. This elevated supply is slowing house price growth and reducing aggressive overbidding, acting as a headwind for new residential development by compressing the margins or perceived value of new builds relative to existing properties, thus dampening overall price momentum.
forces.source_title: More Dutch housing supply pushes transactions to record highs

forces.title: Higher mortgage rates reduce affordability and borrowing capacity
forces.description: Higher mortgage rates, exemplified by the average 10-year fixed rate reaching 4.0% in the Netherlands, are acting as a cyclical headwind on residential real estate. This increases monthly payments for buyers and reduces their maximum borrowing capacity, directly curbing demand and putting downward pressure on house prices. While rates are expected to remain stable without further geopolitical re-escalation, their elevated level continues to constrain market activity for developers.
forces.source_title: More Dutch housing supply pushes transactions to record highs

forces.title: Taxation and rent-cap policies constrain housing investment
forces.description: Taxation and rent-cap policies in Ireland are identified as significant headwinds constraining investment in residential development. While overall construction activity is strengthening, these policies specifically impact the housing segment, limiting the financial attractiveness for developers and investors. Despite strong underlying demand for housing, these regulatory measures are hindering the supply of new units and contributing to the segment being the weakest-performing within the broader construction sector.

forces.title: Execution bottlenecks delay residential new-build projects
forces.description: Execution constraints, including grid congestion and nitrogen restrictions, are increasingly prominent bottlenecks delaying new residential development projects in the Netherlands. These issues prolong delivery times and increase the number of permitted homes awaiting construction starts. Such delays are expected to constrain residential development more frequently in the coming years, hindering supply growth and exacerbating housing shortages, despite increasing demand.
forces.source_title: Recovery in Dutch commercial real estate is less robust than it appears

forces.title: AI transforming real estate value chain and construction efficiency
forces.description: Artificial Intelligence is poised to unlock up to $550 billion in annual value globally across the real estate industry, fundamentally transforming the housing sector. AI applications can enhance customer experience from discovery to service, streamline design and scheduling in construction, and optimize sales, financing, and maintenance workflows. Companies redesigning entire business domains with AI, moving beyond isolated tools, are seeing 10-30% improvements in outcomes like NOI, operating costs, and cycle times.

forces.title: Lack of visibility for HOA sustainability efforts weakens investment
forces.description: For 19% of Dutch homes in HOAs, sustainable renovation efforts are largely invisible to buyers, meaning their value is not reflected in property prices. This lack of transparency weakens incentives for HOAs and individual members to invest time and effort in preparing future renovation measures, despite clear financial benefits from improved energy labels. Consequently, crucial sustainability investments are postponed, hindering the pace of energy transition in collective residential buildings.
forces.source_title: The hidden value of sustainability efforts in Dutch HOAs

forces.title: Short-term rentals reduce available housing supply
forces.description: Short-term rental platforms like Airbnb are estimated to remove approximately 5,000 homes (0.8% of the rental stock) from the regular housing supply in key Belgian cities like Brussels, Antwerp, and Ghent. This significantly adds pressure to an already tight housing market, particularly rental markets, contributing to housing affordability challenges. While new European regulations aim to bring some homes back, the impact on overall affordability will remain limited without addressing structural issues.
forces.source_title: Airbnb only part of Belgium’s housing affordability problem

forces.title: Low construction activity and declining apartment permits exacerbate mismatch
forces.description: Belgium's residential construction is severely constrained by historically low building permits, with overall permits declining for several years and apartment permits falling sharply by 8% YoY in 2025. This sustained downturn in new construction, especially for apartments, directly conflicts with demographic trends indicating a rising demand for smaller, more affordable housing units, leading to a widening supply-demand mismatch and worsening housing affordability.
forces.source_title: Airbnb only part of Belgium’s housing affordability problem

forces.title: Rising construction and financing costs weigh on new housing
forces.description: Increased energy prices, more expensive building materials, and elevated long-term interest rates are significantly driving up costs for both residential developers and potential buyers in Belgium. This 'rising costs' environment makes new construction projects less financially viable for developers, contributing to a slowdown in housing supply and an increase in construction sector bankruptcies, further exacerbating the housing affordability crisis.
forces.source_title: Airbnb only part of Belgium’s housing affordability problem

forces.title: High construction costs delay new home projects in Norway
forces.description: Persistently high construction costs continue to dampen new home construction across most of Norway, resulting in frequent project postponements. Developers and contacts in the industry point to these elevated costs as a primary barrier, hindering the supply of new housing units. This widespread delay contributes to low construction activity, with only the South-West region showing a localized upturn in residential construction, offsetting a broadly weak national outlook.
forces.source_title: Regional Network report 1/2026: Minor changes in growth prospects

forces.title: Weak financial viability limits affordable rental housing investment
forces.description: The growth potential for investment in affordable rental housing in the Netherlands is severely limited due to weak financial viability. A combination of higher interest rates, adverse fiscal changes, and rental regulations makes it less attractive for investors to hold and rent out properties. Instead, many investors prefer to sell existing rental units to owner-occupiers, leading to a reduced supply of affordable rental housing and hindering new investment.
forces.source_title: Recovery in Dutch commercial real estate is less robust than it appears

viewpoints.title: Europe's residential recovery delayed by weak permits and high costs
viewpoints.description: ING Research expects EU construction output to grow by a marginal 0.5% in 2026, with the residential sector remaining a weak spot. Housing permits have stabilized after a 15% rise between summer 2024 and end 2025, delaying a stronger residential recovery. This is attributed to higher interest rates making homes less affordable, heightened geopolitical uncertainty deterring buyers, and increased energy prices pushing up material costs. The business case for new housing projects remains difficult for developers.
viewpoints.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

viewpoints.title: Belgian residential permit recovery faces headwinds despite initial growth
viewpoints.description: ING Research observes a welcome improvement in Belgian building permits for new residential construction, increasing by 14% year-on-year in H1 2026, with apartment permits up 8%. However, this recovery faces significant challenges. Higher energy prices are driving up material costs, worsening financing conditions due to rising mortgage rates are reducing affordability, and order books have weakened since July. Policy uncertainty from increased registration duties also dampens demand.
viewpoints.source_title: Belgian building permit recovery continues, but challenges lie ahead

viewpoints.title: Belgian housing market to gradually cool despite Q2 resilience
viewpoints.description: ING Research expects the Belgian housing market to gradually cool, with nominal median house prices increasing by 2.5% in 2026 and 2.0% in 2027. Despite surprising resilience in Q2 2026 with modest price increases and transaction recovery, weaker mortgage lending and persistently higher interest rates point to slowing momentum. Additionally, higher energy prices are expected to widen the value gap for energy-efficient homes, shifting demand.
viewpoints.source_title: Second-quarter resilience masks a more challenging outlook for Belgian housing

viewpoints.title: Dutch housing permits at 10-year high, but construction recovery limited
viewpoints.description: ING Research reports Dutch housing permits hit a 10-year high in May 2026, suggesting a gradual recovery for housing construction. However, the recovery will remain modest, with 71,000 new-build homes expected in 2026 and 74,000 in 2027, following a 7% decline in H1 2026. This limited growth is due to housing starts trailing permits and persistent challenges from high construction costs, staff shortages, and nitrogen restrictions delaying projects.
viewpoints.source_title: Dutch housing permits hit 10-year high, but construction still slow off the…

viewpoints.title: Record Dutch existing home sales, but price growth to moderate
viewpoints.description: ING Research forecasts Dutch existing home sales to reach a record 245,000 in 2026, slightly easing to 240,000 in 2027, driven by increasing supply. However, house price growth is expected to moderate to 3% in 2026 and 1.5% in 2027 due to this increased supply (including former rental properties), higher mortgage rates, and weaker sentiment. Offsets include a tight market, rising household incomes, and additional financial support for first-time buyers.
viewpoints.source_title: More Dutch housing supply pushes transactions to record highs

viewpoints.title: Irish housing segment weakest amid construction growth
viewpoints.description: Allianz IE indicates that while Ireland's overall construction activity is strengthening, housing remains the weakest-performing segment. Investment in residential development is constrained by taxation and rent-cap policies in some areas. Despite these policy-induced headwinds, underlying demand for housing is strong and is anticipated to support activity over the longer term, suggesting a bifurcated outlook within the broader construction sector.

viewpoints.title: Dutch affordable rental housing investment limited by weak viability
viewpoints.description: ING Research notes that the growth potential for investment in affordable rental housing in the Netherlands is limited due to weak financial viability. Current residential transactions are dominated by investors selling older rental properties to owner-occupiers, a more attractive option given higher interest rates, fiscal changes, and rental regulations. Furthermore, new residential development faces constraints from execution bottlenecks like grid congestion and nitrogen restrictions, delaying project delivery and increasing construction costs.
viewpoints.source_title: Recovery in Dutch commercial real estate is less robust than it appears

viewpoints.title: Belgium's housing affordability crisis driven by structural bottlenecks
viewpoints.description: ING Research attributes Belgium's housing affordability problems primarily to structural bottlenecks, with short-term rentals like Airbnb only a contributing factor. Key issues include historically low building permits, a worsening mismatch where apartment permits decline despite rising demand for smaller units, and increasing construction and financing costs. Additionally, restrictive regulatory frameworks, such as rent caps, are inadvertently reducing rental supply and dampening new construction, highlighting the need for a stable investment climate.
viewpoints.source_title: Airbnb only part of Belgium’s housing affordability problem

viewpoints.title: Norway's new residential construction continues to be postponed
viewpoints.description: Norges Bank reports that new residential construction activity remains low across Norway, with a widespread delay in project upturns. This is primarily due to higher interest rates and persistent expectations of rising building costs. While the South-West region is an exception, showing some growth in residential construction, the national outlook remains challenged by financial viability concerns for new builds and general dampening of construction sector growth.
viewpoints.source_title: Regional Network report 2/2026: Recruitment difficulties have eased somewhat

viewpoints.title: French construction output facing contraction due to weak housing
viewpoints.description: ING Research forecasts a 2.5% contraction in France's construction output in 2026, following a 3.5% fall in 2025. This negative outlook is driven by weakened sector confidence and housing permits remaining below previous year's levels. Developers face significant challenges as existing-home prices remain low, limiting their ability to pass on higher material costs, making many new residential projects unprofitable and leading to postponements.
viewpoints.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

viewpoints.title: Spanish construction recovering, supported by robust GDP growth
viewpoints.description: ING Research forecasts a 3% growth in Spain's construction sector for 2026, indicating a continued recovery after a significant decline between 2019 and 2022. Building permits have risen sharply in recent years, though their momentum is now easing. Despite this, robust GDP growth is expected to provide ongoing support for construction activities, including residential projects, in the current and upcoming year.
viewpoints.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

viewpoints.title: German construction sector expected to recover in 2026
viewpoints.description: ING Research anticipates Germany's construction sector to resume growth in 2026, marking a recovery after five consecutive years of contraction and a more than 10% decline between 2020 and 2025. This modest rebound, supported by developments in housing and infrastructure, is expected to gradually gain momentum into 2027. Government initiatives like the 'housing construction turbo' aim to accelerate planning and approvals, though local implementation remains a factor.
viewpoints.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

viewpoints.title: Belgium's housing supply-demand mismatch worsened in 2025
viewpoints.description: ING Research reports that Belgium's housing supply-demand mismatch widened further in 2025, driven by a sustained downturn in residential building permits. Total permits declined 3% in 2025, with apartment permits falling sharply by almost 8% YoY, contrasting with demographic trends showing increased demand for smaller units. With overall permit levels historically low and interest rates expected to trend upwards, a strong rebound in construction is unlikely in the near term, exacerbating affordability issues.
viewpoints.source_title: Belgium’s housing supply–demand mismatch widened further in 2025

First-time buyers are contributing more of their own funds, and municipalities are providing increasing numbers of loans via the Dutch Municipal Housing Incentive Fund (SVn).

Providing subsidies and attractive loan options for less energy-efficient HOAs with limited financial means can unlock necessary sustainability investments.

new_opportunities.description: Linking sustainability obligations to natural maintenance moments in long-term plans for HOA buildings can accelerate the pace of renovation where collective agreement is challenging.
